questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Kenya?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Kenya article.

questions.proof: Its capital city is Nairobi, which is the 14th largest city in Africa (after Accra, Ghana).

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Kenya?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Kenya on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Kenya article.

questions.proof: To the north, it borders Ethiopia; to the northwest, it borders South Sudan; to the south, Tanzania; and to the west, Uganda and Lake Victoria.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Kenya?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Languages” part of the Kenya article.

questions.proof: English and Swahili are Kenya's official languages.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Kenya is bordered by the Indian Ocean and the Jubaland part of _____ to its east.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “part”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Kenya article.

questions.proof: Kenya is bordered by the Indian Ocean and the Jubaland part of Somalia to its east.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It is about the size of _____, and almost as large as the U.S. state of Texas.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “size”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Kenya article.

questions.proof: It is about the size of France, and almost as large as the U.S. state of Texas.
